original_interpretation: Micron recorded inventory write-downs of US$1.43 billion in its fiscal second quarter of 2023 (quarter ended 2 March 2023).
evidence_found: "Inventory write-downs of $1.43 billion, impact of $1.34 per diluted share"; quarter ended March 2, 2023 (Micron Q2 FY2023 8-K Ex. 99.1, highlights)

original_interpretation: Micron's GAAP gross margin was negative 32.7% in fiscal Q2 2023, on revenue of US$3.69 billion versus US$7.79 billion a year earlier.
evidence_found: "Revenue of $3.69 billion versus $4.09 billion for the prior quarter and $7.79 billion for the same period last year"; gross margin $(1,206) million, "(32.7%)" of revenue, GAAP column (Q2 FY2023 8-K Ex. 99.1, financial summary)

original_interpretation: Micron's fiscal 2023 revenue was US$15.54 billion, down from US$30.76 billion in fiscal 2022.
evidence_found: Full-year revenue "$15,540" million FY2023 vs "$30,758" million FY2022; fiscal year ended "August 31, 2023" (Q4 FY2023 8-K Ex. 99.1, financial summary table)
notes: FY2023 ended 31 Aug 2023; metric period 'Aug/Sep 2023' can be tightened to 31 Aug 2023.

original_interpretation: Micron's fiscal 2023 GAAP gross margin was negative 9.1% and its GAAP net loss was US$5.83 billion.
evidence_found: FY2023 GAAP gross margin "(9.1%)" (vs 45.2% FY2022); net loss "$(5,833)" million, diluted EPS "$(5.34)" (Q4 FY2023 8-K Ex. 99.1, full-year column)

original_interpretation: Micron's inventory write-downs in fiscal 2023 were US$1.43 billion in Q2 and US$401 million in Q3, about US$1.83 billion in total.
evidence_found: Reconciliation lists inventory write-down provisions of $1.43 billion (Q2 FY23), $401 million (Q3 FY23), $0 (Q4 FY23); full-year total $1.831 billion (Q4 FY2023 8-K Ex. 99.1, non-GAAP reconciliation)
notes: Sum of 1.43+0.401=1.831 matches the release's full-year total.

original_interpretation: Micron's net investments in capital expenditures were US$7.01 billion in fiscal 2023.
evidence_found: "Investments in capital expenditures, net(2) were $1.01 billion for the fourth quarter of 2023 and $7.01 billion for the full year of 2023" (Q4 FY2023 8-K Ex. 99.1)

original_interpretation: In November 2022 Micron announced it was cutting DRAM and NAND wafer starts by about 20% versus its fiscal Q4 2022 and expected negative DRAM bit supply growth in calendar 2023.
evidence_found: "cutting DRAM and NAND wafer starts by 20 percent compared to its prior quarter"; Micron anticipates "year-on-year bit supply growth will be negative for DRAM, and in the single-digit percentage range for NAND" (Blocks and Files, 16 Nov 2022). Also cross-checked against Micron's own 16 Nov 2022 GlobeNewswire release (reproduced at stocks.observer-reporter.com/observerreporter/article/gnwcq-2022-11-16-micron-announces-further-actions-to-address-market-conditions): "reducing DRAM and NAND wafer starts by approximately 20% versus fiscal fourth quarter 2022"; "In calendar 2023, Micron now expects its year-on-year bit supply growth to be negative for DRAM"
notes: Micron's own release confirms the FQ4-22 baseline and calendar-2023 framing; a company-release source could be added to raise the evidence tier.

original_interpretation: Blocks and Files reported that Micron's November 2022 plan implied a capex cut of close to 50% with further cuts being worked on.
evidence_found: "make a near 50 percent cut in Capex spending" is described as having been decided previously (at the end of the prior quarter); "Micron is also working toward additional capex cuts, implying more than the 50 percent already decided" (Blocks and Files, 16 Nov 2022). Micron's own 16 Nov 2022 release only says "Micron is also working toward additional capex cuts" with no percentage.
correction: The near-50% capex cut was, per Blocks and Files, an earlier decision (end of the prior quarter, i.e. Micron's Sept 2022 FQ4 update), not part of the November 2022 plan; the November announcement added unquantified further capex cuts. Micron's own November release gives no capex percentage.
notes: Researcher's note already flags that the ~50% may refer to WFE capex; not resolved here.

original_interpretation: SK hynix reported 2023 revenue of KRW 32.77 trillion, an operating loss of KRW 7.73 trillion (margin -24%) and a net loss of KRW 9.14 trillion.
evidence_found: "Revenues for 2023 at 32.77 trillion won, operating loss at 7.73 trillion won"; "operating profit margin at negative 24%"; net loss "9.14 trillion won" (SK hynix release, 25 Jan 2024, PR Newswire reproduction)
notes: Source is a third-party reproduction of the company release.

original_interpretation: SK hynix returned to an operating profit of KRW 346 billion in Q4 2023 after four consecutive quarterly losses.
evidence_found: "recorded an operating profit of 346 billion won in the fourth quarter", "the first quarter of profit following four straight quarters of losses" (SK hynix release, 25 Jan 2024)

original_interpretation: For 2024 SK hynix said it would minimise any increase in capital expenditure and, in NAND where recovery was slower, prioritised streamlining investments and costs.
evidence_found: "minimizing an increase in capital expenditure for a stable operation"; in NAND "prioritized streamlining investments and costs" (SK hynix release, 25 Jan 2024)

original_interpretation: In its 1Q 2023 pre-earnings guidance (7 April 2023) Samsung Electronics guided consolidated operating profit of about KRW 0.6 trillion and said it planned to cut production of memory products for which supply had been secured.
evidence_found: "Consolidated operating profit: Approximately 0.6 trillion Korean won" (sales approx. 63 trillion won); "However, as we have now achieved sufficient supply capability for certain products, we plan to cut production of those products while maintaining our ongoing efforts to prepare for the future" (Samsung 1Q 2023 pre-earnings guidance, 7 Apr 2023)
notes: Source wording is 'achieved sufficient supply capability for certain products' (memory context), which the claim paraphrases as 'supply had been secured'. Guidance is preliminary, not final results.

original_interpretation: Kioxia announced on 30 September 2022 that it would reduce wafer starts at its Yokkaichi and Kitakami flash memory plants by about 30% from October 2022.
evidence_found: "...will reduce its wafer start production volume by approximately 30 percent, starting from October this year"; applies to Yokkaichi and Kitakami plants (Kioxia news release, 30 Sep 2022)

original_interpretation: TrendForce forecast (July 2026) that conventional DRAM contract prices would rise 13-18% QoQ and NAND flash contract prices 10-15% QoQ in 3Q26, a slowdown from earlier quarters.
evidence_found: "Conventional DRAM contract prices are forecast to rise 13–18% QoQ in 3Q26"; "NAND Flash contract prices are projected to increase by 10–15% QoQ"; "a noticeably slower pace than in previous quarters" (TrendForce, 3 Jul 2026)

original_interpretation: TrendForce states that server DRAM price gains in 3Q26 are moderated because a portion of procurement is governed by long-term supply agreements (LTAs).
evidence_found: "While server DRAM will remain undersupplied in the third quarter, pricing gains are expected to moderate as a portion of procurement is governed by long-term supply agreements (LTAs)." (TrendForce, 3 Jul 2026)

original_interpretation: On 2 February 2026 TrendForce raised its 1Q26 forecast for conventional DRAM contract prices from +55-60% to +90-95% QoQ and for NAND flash from +33-38% to +55-60% QoQ.
evidence_found: Conventional DRAM "revised upward, from a previous estimate of 55–60% to now 90–95%"; NAND Flash "now expected to rise from 33–38% to 55–60%" (TrendForce, 2 Feb 2026)
notes: Forecast as of Feb 2026; TrendForce later (1 Jun 2026, SRC-0361) reported actual 1Q26 conventional DRAM contract prices up ~93–98% (CLM-1135).

original_interpretation: TrendForce projected PC DRAM contract prices to rise more than 100% QoQ in 1Q26, a record quarterly increase, with server and mobile DRAM around 90%.
evidence_found: PC DRAM "expected to increase by over 100% QoQ in 1Q26, setting a new record"; server DRAM "up by around 90% QoQ in 1Q26"; mobile DRAM "surge by around 90% QoQ in 1Q26" (TrendForce, 2 Feb 2026)

original_interpretation: TrendForce reported that conventional DRAM contract prices rose about 93-98% QoQ in 1Q26 and DRAM industry revenue rose 81% QoQ to US$97 billion.
evidence_found: "conventional DRAM ... increased by approximately 93% to 98% QoQ"; "overall industry revenue increase of 81% QoQ, reaching $97 billion" (TrendForce, 1 Jun 2026)
correction: Numbers verified. The metric population 'incl. HBM' is not stated in the release; the release does not say whether the $97bn DRAM industry revenue includes HBM.
notes: Population field should read 'DRAM industry revenue as defined by TrendForce (HBM inclusion not stated in release)'.

original_interpretation: TrendForce forecast (June 2026) that conventional DRAM contract prices would rise another 58-63% QoQ in 2Q26.
evidence_found: "conventional DRAM contract prices to rise another 58–63% QoQ in 2Q26" (TrendForce, 1 Jun 2026)

original_interpretation: TrendForce reported conventional DRAM contract prices rose 45-50% QoQ in 4Q25 (50-55% including HBM) and DRAM industry revenue rose 29.4% to US$53.58 billion.
evidence_found: "total DRAM industry revenue to $53.58 billion in 4Q25, up 29.4% QoQ"; "Conventional DRAM contract prices rose 45–50% QoQ"; "blended contract prices for conventional DRAM and HBM increased 50–55%" (TrendForce, 26 Feb 2026)

original_interpretation: TrendForce reported in November 2025 that DRAM pricing had shifted from quarterly frameworks to monthly quotes and that Samsung had largely halted contract offers.
evidence_found: "The pricing cycle has also shifted from quarterly frameworks to monthly quotes, according to TrendForce."; "Currently, Samsung has largely halted contract offers, while other suppliers have adopted a wait-and-see stance." Headline: "DRAM Quotes Reportedly Shift to Monthly as Samsung Largely Halts Contracts"; article cites Commercial Times (8 Oct 2025) and TechNews (1 Nov 2025) (TrendForce News, 3 Nov 2025)
correction: The monthly-quote shift is attributed to TrendForce; the Samsung contract halt is presented as a media report ('reportedly', citing Commercial Times/TechNews), not a TrendForce finding. Claim should attribute the Samsung part to press reports carried by TrendForce News.
notes: TrendForce News is TrendForce's news desk that aggregates press reports, distinct from TrendForce research press releases.

original_interpretation: Micron confirmed in June 2025 that it had sent end-of-life notices for DDR4 and LPDDR4 to PC and data-center customers.
evidence_found: "Micron's EVP confirmed the company has sent end-of-life (EOL) notices for DDR4 and LPDDR4 to PC and data center customers." (TrendForce News, 13 Jun 2025, citing IT Home, MoneyDJ, Nikkei, Etnews)
notes: Secondhand: TrendForce News relaying media reports of the Micron executive's statement. Article also says supply continues to automotive, industrial and networking customers.

original_interpretation: Industry reports in June 2025 said Micron raised June DDR4 prices by 50% and some DDR4 quotes jumped as much as 100% after the end-of-life notices.
evidence_found: "recent rumors say Micron has hiked June DDR4 prices by 50%, sending 8Gb and 16Gb spot prices soaring"; "industry sources indicate that DDR4 pricing is in chaos, with some quotes jumping as much as 100%" (TrendForce News, 13 Jun 2025)
correction: The 50% Micron DDR4 price hike is described by the source as a rumor, not a confirmed report; the 100% figure is from unnamed industry sources about DDR4 quotes generally, not tied to Micron.
notes: Keep as reported_claim; should not be used as a confirmed Micron price action.

original_interpretation: In September 2025 Micron said it had six HBM customers and had pricing agreements with almost all of them for the vast majority of its calendar-2026 HBM3E supply.
evidence_found: Micron "now has six customers for its HBM products, almost all of which have agreed to 'pricing agreements … for a vast majority of our HBM3E supply in calendar 2026.'" (The Register, 24 Sep 2025)
notes: Source is news (tier 3) quoting company remarks; Micron's own FQ4 2025 materials would be a stronger source.

original_interpretation: SK hynix said in October 2025 that HBM supply discussions for 2026 were completed and it had secured customer demand for its entire 2026 DRAM and NAND production.
evidence_found: "HBM supply discussion for next year completed"; "already secured full customer demand for its entire DRAM and NAND production for next year" (SK hynix 3Q25 release, 29 Oct 2025)

original_interpretation: SK hynix reported 3Q25 revenue of KRW 24.4489 trillion and operating profit of KRW 11.3834 trillion.
evidence_found: "24.4489 trillion won in revenues, 11.3834 trillion won in operating profit" (SK hynix 3Q25 release, 29 Oct 2025)

original_interpretation: Micron reported fiscal Q3 2026 revenue of US$41.46 billion (US$9.30 billion a year earlier) and a GAAP gross margin of 84.6%.
evidence_found: "Revenue of $41.46 billion versus $23.86 billion for the prior quarter and $9.30 billion for the same period last year"; gross margin GAAP "84.6%" (non-GAAP "84.9%"); quarter ended May 28, 2026 (Q3 FY2026 8-K Ex. 99.1)

original_interpretation: Micron guided fiscal Q4 2026 revenue of US$50.0 billion plus or minus US$1.0 billion at about 86% gross margin.
evidence_found: Outlook: revenue "$50.0 billion ± $1.0 billion"; gross margin approximately 86% (GAAP and non-GAAP) (Q3 FY2026 8-K Ex. 99.1, guidance table)
notes: Guidance. Micron's FQ4 2026 actual results were scheduled for release on 30 Sep 2026 and were not yet available at check time; re-check after release.

original_interpretation: Micron's Q3 FY2026 release says it executed Strategic Customer Agreements that it expects to enhance the durability and predictability of its financial performance.
evidence_found: Headline bullet "Micron executes transformational Strategic Customer Agreements"; CEO quote: "We believe our multi-year Strategic Customer Agreements will significantly enhance the durability and predictability of Micron's strong financial performance." (Q3 FY2026 8-K Ex. 99.1)
notes: The durability statement is the CEO's belief ('We believe'), correctly typed as reported_claim.

original_interpretation: Micron said in June 2026 that it had signed 16 Strategic Customer Agreements representing roughly 20% of its DRAM volume and one-third of its NAND volume.
evidence_found: "As a result, Micron has signed 16 strategic customer agreements (SCA) for memory supply, representing roughly 20 percent of its DRAM volume and a third of its NAND volume over this period." (Blocks and Files, 25 Jun 2026)
correction: The 20% DRAM / one-third NAND shares are 'over this period', i.e. over the agreements' multi-year terms, not a share of current-quarter volume; claim omits this qualifier.
notes: Secondhand (industry press reporting the earnings call).

original_interpretation: Micron's Strategic Customer Agreements run five years for data-center and consumer customers and three years for automotive customers.
evidence_found: "They cover the datacenter and consumer markets (5-year duration) and also the automotive sector (3 year duration)." (Blocks and Files, 25 Jun 2026)

original_interpretation: Micron said its largest Strategic Customer Agreements generally cap prices of existing products at the calendar Q2 2026 market price and set a floor price for the term.
evidence_found: "The largest agreements generally have a ceiling price for existing products at the current CQ2 (calendar Q2) market price, and a floor price through the term of the agreement" (Blocks and Files, 25 Jun 2026, attributed to CEO Sanjay Mehrotra)
